sections.title: Morphology
sections.text: Candida parapsilosis is a yeast with cells that may be round, oval, or cylindrical and reproduce by budding. Depending on strain and culture conditions, it can also form pseudohyphae: chains of elongated cells with constrictions at the septa. Sources describe white to cream colonies that may be smooth or wrinkled. This species does not form true hyphae.

sections.title: Ecology and medical significance
sections.text: The review devoted to C. parapsilosis describes it as a commensal yeast of human skin, with pathogenicity limited when the skin barrier is intact. It is also recognized as a cause of invasive infections, especially in some healthcare settings. It can adhere to prosthetic devices and catheters and form biofilms.

sections.title: Scope and safety
sections.text: This entry concerns a microscopic yeast, not a mushroom for collection. Cell forms, colony colour, and pseudohyphae vary with strain and conditions and cannot by themselves identify a species. Identification requires microbiological testing. Edibility is not assessed here.

traits: Unicellular yeast; cells round, oval, or cylindrical, reproducing by budding
May form pseudohyphae of elongated cells; does not form true hyphae
Culture colonies generally white to cream; smooth, wrinkled, or otherwise variable by strain and conditions
Commensal of human skin that can also cause opportunistic invasive infections
Associated with prosthetic devices and catheters; can adhere to them and form biofilms
safetyNote: Microbiology reference, not a foraging or food entry. Microscopic appearance or colony morphology alone cannot identify C. parapsilosis. Suspected infection requires assessment by a healthcare professional and appropriate laboratory testing.
